## Excursions to Laguna Colorada: flamingos and Bolivia's red lagoon

[Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/) is on the high-altitude plateau of southwestern Bolivia. Its water takes on reddish-brown tones, and flocks of flamingos can be seen in the shallows. The color changes with the light and natural conditions, so the lagoon will not always appear the same vivid scarlet.

The lake lies in the [Eduardo Avaroa Andean Fauna National Reserve](/bolivia/place/eduardo-avaroa-national-reserve/). This area is renowned for its combination of mineral lagoons, deserts, geothermal fields and mountain landscapes. Travelers explore it by four-wheel-drive vehicles, connecting Laguna Colorada with other stops. Before choosing an excursion, it helps to know where it starts and where it ends.

## What to see near the red lagoon

The lake is one of the main places to observe high-altitude Andean flamingos. The birds feed in shallow water, but it is impossible to predict how close they will be to the road. Observe them from a distance to avoid disturbing wildlife.

Nearby lies the [Siloli Desert](/bolivia/place/siloli-desert/). Farther along the nature routes are the [Sol de Mañana geyser field](/bolivia/place/sol-de-manana-geysers/), [Polques Hot Springs](/bolivia/place/polques-hot-springs/) and [Laguna Verde](/bolivia/place/laguna-verde/). These sights are spread across a vast area: mentioning them together in a geographic description does not mean every excursion visits them all.

Bolivia's national tourism authority highlights Colorada and Verde as distinctive natural attractions of the reserve, noting its colored lagoons, geysers and high-altitude wildlife.

## Which excursions does Ada Tours offer?

On the [two-day four-wheel-drive tour from Uyuni](/bolivia/uyuni/uyuni-salt-flats-4x4-tour-2-days/), Laguna Colorada is visited on the first day along with Laguna Verde, the Dalí Desert, Polques Springs and Sol de Mañana. On day two, the route continues past smaller lagoons to the [Uyuni Salt Flats](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). An overnight stay in an expedition-style hotel is included. Here the red lagoon forms part of a longer journey.

["Eduardo Avaroa: Red and Green Lagoons"](/bolivia/ojo-de-perdiz/eduardo-avaroa-colorada-verde-uyuni/) is a separate full-day excursion module. It starts at Ojo de Perdiz, passes the Stone Tree and Siloli Desert on the way to Laguna Colorada, then continues to the geysers, Polques and Laguna Verde. The excursion ends with a transfer toward Uyuni. **There is no crossing into Chile on this route.**

Another option is ["Across the Bolivian Altiplano to San Pedro de Atacama"](/bolivia/uyuni/uyuni-altiplano-border-transfer/). Laguna Colorada is visited on the way to the geysers, springs and Chilean border, with a total transfer time of approximately 8–9 hours. Choose this option when the nature excursion also connects [Bolivia](/bolivia/) with [northern Chile](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/).

| Excursion | Where the route leads |
|---|---|
| Two days from Uyuni | Lagoons and salt flats |
| Eduardo Avaroa | Colorada, Verde and Uyuni |
| Transfer into Chile | Altiplano and border |

There is also the ["Altiplano: Five Lagoons, Colorada and Transfer to Chile" excursion](/bolivia/uyuni/altiplano-lagoons-chalviri-chile-border/). In addition to the red lagoon, it visits Kiar Kkota, Hedionda, Cañapa, Honda and Ramaditas, before continuing to Chalviri and the border. Choose between these routes based on their number of stops and direction of travel, rather than a shared photograph of the red lake.

## How much time do you need and how should you prepare?

The lagoon lies at high altitude in the cold, dry Altiplano climate. Travelers spend considerable time in vehicles, stop at windy viewpoints and experience temperature changes between sun and shade. Warm clothes, UV protection, water and comfortable shoes are essential even for short stops.

Without adequate acclimatization, altitude sickness symptoms are possible. Discuss the route and your health beforehand, especially if arriving directly from low elevations. At geothermal sites, stay within marked safe areas and follow your guides' instructions.

Road conditions and the order of visits can depend on rainfall and the state of the ground. Seeing Laguna Colorada does not guarantee a particular driving speed between the other lagoons.

## Frequently asked questions about Laguna Colorada

### Why is the water sometimes red?

Its color is associated with microorganisms and the lake's mineral environment. The apparent shade also depends on light and wind.

### Can you see flamingos on a trip to Colorada?

Yes, it is a well-known flamingo habitat. But their numbers and distance from visitors depend on natural conditions, so close-up photographs cannot be guaranteed.

### Is Laguna Verde included in the excursion?

It is included in these [Ada Tours itineraries](/bolivia/ojo-de-perdiz/eduardo-avaroa-colorada-verde-uyuni/). Check the actual stops separately when considering a different route.

### Does the excursion necessarily end in Chile?

No. Some itineraries continue toward Uyuni, while others cross the border and end in San Pedro de Atacama. This is a major distinction when planning the rest of your journey.

## Excursions to Laguna Verde: a turquoise lake below Licancabur

[Laguna Verde](/bolivia/place/laguna-verde/) lies among volcanic slopes in southwestern Bolivia, near the Chilean border. The cone of Licancabur rises above the lake, whose water takes on greenish and turquoise hues under certain conditions. It is one of the most recognizable landscapes of the high-altitude desert.

The lagoon is in the [Eduardo Avaroa reserve](/bolivia/place/eduardo-avaroa-national-reserve/) area and is rarely the only destination on a journey. Itineraries connect it with [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/), geothermal fields and the Uyuni Salt Flats, or use it as one of the final stops before crossing into Chile.

## Why is the lake green?

The mineral content of the water and wind affect its color. Depending on the light, the same surface may appear vivid turquoise, pale or almost gray. The name "Green Lagoon" identifies the geographic feature; it is not a promise of brightly colored water in every photograph.

This is not a place for ordinary swimming. It is a high-altitude mineral lagoon visited for its landscape and views of the volcano. Nearby tourist stops are in the cold, windy, dry Altiplano.

The same natural region contains [Sol de Mañana](/bolivia/place/sol-de-manana-geysers/) and other geothermal attractions, but separate road journeys are needed between them. Bolivia's official tourism authority describes Laguna Verde as part of reserve routes to geysers and hot springs.

## Ada Tours trips to Laguna Verde

On the ["Uyuni in 2 Days: Lagoons, Geysers and Salt Flats by 4x4" excursion](/bolivia/uyuni/uyuni-salt-flats-4x4-tour-2-days/), Laguna Verde is visited at the start of day one. Travelers then see the Dalí Desert, [Polques](/bolivia/place/polques-hot-springs/), [Sol de Mañana](/bolivia/place/sol-de-manana-geysers/) and Laguna Colorada. After the overnight stay, the program continues to smaller lagoons and the salt flats. This itinerary links the remote Altiplano landscapes with Bolivia's principal salt plateau.

The ["Eduardo Avaroa: Red and Green Lagoons" excursion](/bolivia/ojo-de-perdiz/eduardo-avaroa-colorada-verde-uyuni/) begins at Ojo de Perdiz and travels through the Siloli Desert, Laguna Colorada, the geysers and the hot springs. Laguna Verde marks the end of the nature portion, followed by a transfer to Uyuni. **This itinerary does not cross into Chile.**

The ["Across the Bolivian Altiplano to San Pedro de Atacama" transfer](/bolivia/uyuni/uyuni-altiplano-border-transfer/) also includes Laguna Verde but serves a different purpose: it ends in [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/) after crossing the border. With sightseeing stops, the drive in our itinerary takes about 8–9 hours. Consider this option if you plan to continue from Bolivia into northern Chile.

| Option | What happens after Laguna Verde |
|---|---|
| Uyuni in 2 days | Continue through Bolivia |
| Eduardo Avaroa | Transfer toward Uyuni |
| Altiplano to Chile | Border crossing |

## What else can you see on the same route?

At [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/), the main natural sights are reddish water and flamingos; at Verde, attention is drawn to the shape of Licancabur volcano and the turquoise lake. These are separate lakes in different locations.

Another characteristic stop is the [Sol de Mañana geothermal field](/bolivia/place/sol-de-manana-geysers/), where steam jets and heat-altered ground are visible. [Polques](/bolivia/place/polques-hot-springs/) is known for hot springs. Whether swimming is possible and the time allocated to a stop depend on the excursion's terms, not merely on the presence of springs.

On some roads to the reserve, travelers visit the [Siloli Desert](/bolivia/place/siloli-desert/) and wind-shaped rock formations. When choosing a program, compare how many of these places are actually included and which lie in the direction of onward travel.

## Altitude, weather and crossing into Chile

The excursion takes place at high altitude. Temperatures can be low even under bright sun, while winds beside the exposed lake can be strong. Bring warm layers, wind and sun protection, water and maintain a sensible pace of physical effort.

For a trip across the Chilean border, separately check travel documents, border-post hours and road access. The terms of an "Uyuni–Chile" transfer must not be applied to every tour featuring Laguna Verde: some itineraries return to Bolivia.

If you feel unwell at altitude, tell your companions rather than pushing on to see one more viewpoint. Preparing for long journeys at high elevations is part of choosing the excursion.

## Frequently asked questions about Laguna Verde

### Is the water green all day?

No. Its shade changes with the light, wind and natural conditions. Even when the water looks paler, the view of Licancabur remains central to the scenery.

### Can you visit Verde and Colorada together?

Yes. Several [Ada Tours excursions](/bolivia/ojo-de-perdiz/eduardo-avaroa-colorada-verde-uyuni/) combine them. Allow for the distances and length of the journey.

### Do all excursions go into Chile?

No. For example, the [Eduardo Avaroa route](/bolivia/ojo-de-perdiz/eduardo-avaroa-colorada-verde-uyuni/) ends with a Bolivian transfer to Uyuni. Border crossings are included only on certain itineraries.

### Where should you start?

It depends on your wider South America route. Combine the lagoons with [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) if you want to see the salt flats; if you are continuing into the Atacama Desert, choose an excursion that ends in Chile.

## Lake Titicaca excursions in Bolivia: Copacabana and Isla del Sol

[Lake Titicaca](/bolivia/place/lake-titicaca-bolivia/) lies on a high plateau between Bolivia and Peru. Its deep blue waters, island communities, mountain slopes and Andean cultural traditions make a visit a distinct part of a journey.

On the Bolivian shore, [Copacabana](/bolivia/place/copacabana/) is a principal starting point for excursions. Boats depart from here to [Isla del Sol](/bolivia/place/isla-del-sol/), an island linked to Inca origin legends. We offer two ways to experience the lake: **by catamaran** and **by speedboat**.

## What to see on the Bolivian shore

Copacabana is a lakeside town known for its basilica and pilgrimage traditions. Bolivia's official tourism authority highlights trips to Isla del Sol and Isla de la Luna, ancient Andean monuments and the culture of lakeside communities.

Lake Titicaca is approximately **3,812 m above sea level**. Even on a calm boat trip, travelers can feel the altitude: walking to the pier or climbing steps on the island may be harder than in a lowland city. It can be windy on open water and cool in the morning and evening.

On [Isla del Sol](/bolivia/place/isla-del-sol/), visitors discover Inca legends, agricultural terraces, historic structures and lake views. Not every island monument is included on each excursion. Exploring more of the island takes additional time, and the chosen bay and landing point determine which sights are accessible.

## Catamaran: the lake and an Andean ritual

On the ["Titicaca by Catamaran: Copacabana and Isla del Sol" excursion](/bolivia/copacabana/titicaca-isla-del-sol-catamaran/), travelers board a catamaran upon reaching the Bolivian shore and sail to the island. **The program includes the catamaran journey, a symbolic Kallawaya ritual and lunch on the lake.**

This itinerary is included, among others, in the extended "Enchanting Peru and Bolivia" journey. After the island section, travelers continue by road to La Paz. Interpreter assistance during the crossing **is not included** in that particular tour's price, an important condition when choosing.

A catamaran is suitable if the journey across the lake and the organized cultural program are substantial parts of your day. But the vessel name does not tell you the exact number of hours on the island, list of archaeological sites or additional services; the specific excursion description determines those.

## Speedboat: Copacabana and Isla del Sol

["Titicaca: Copacabana and Isla del Sol by Speedboat"](/bolivia/copacabana/titicaca-isla-del-sol-speedboat/) is another format. From Copacabana, a speedboat takes travelers to Isla del Sol, where they encounter regional traditions and participate in a symbolic Kallawaya ritual with offerings to Pachamama.

The itinerary also includes lunch at a restaurant overlooking the lake. The duration is described as **a full day**. Return to the Bolivian shore and onward road travel depend on the larger tour if this excursion forms part of it.

The main difference between the catamaran and speedboat is the manner of travel and how the program is organized. A "speedboat" does not, by itself, guarantee more time to explore the island. Timing depends on departures, weather and transfer arrangements.

| Option | Distinctive feature |
|---|---|
| Catamaran | Sailing, ritual and lunch |
| Speedboat | Crossing to the island and cultural program |

## Choosing when traveling through Peru and Bolivia

If you are visiting both countries, Titicaca often connects the Peruvian lakeshore, Copacabana and La Paz. But the border crossing, road escort and separate transfers should be considered as part of **the complete tour itinerary**, not assumed to be included in every lake excursion.

First decide your direction of travel: are you coming from Peru into Bolivia, returning to the previous shore or continuing to La Paz? Then compare the exact boat section and cultural activities included on the chosen excursion.

For a broader itinerary, see [Bolivia tours](/bolivia/tour/) and journeys combining [Peru and Bolivia](/multi-country/). Lake Titicaca may be part of a multi-day transfer or occupy a dedicated excursion day.

## Weather and high-altitude lake considerations

Even in clear sunshine, cold winds may sweep across the lake. Bring a warm layer, sun protection and a hat for the boat trip. Comfortable shoes help on the shore and island trails. Be prepared for boat movement and follow the crew's instructions.

If arriving from a much lower elevation, avoid excessive physical exertion immediately upon arrival. Seek medical help if significant altitude sickness symptoms develop. Boat departure times and landing opportunities may depend on lake conditions and local regulations.

## Frequently asked questions about Titicaca excursions

### Is Lake Titicaca in Bolivia or Peru?

Both countries share the lake. This catalog concerns excursions on **the Bolivian side**, mainly from Copacabana to Isla del Sol.

### Which island do both Ada Tours excursions visit?

Both programs visit [Isla del Sol](/bolivia/place/isla-del-sol/). [Isla de la Luna](/bolivia/place/isla-de-la-luna/) is separate and must not be assumed to be included.

### Which is better: catamaran or speedboat?

A catamaran may appeal to travelers who enjoy the sailing experience and onboard program. Choose a speedboat based on the agreed logistics and island visit. Compare actual timing and included services.

### Can you continue to La Paz?

Yes, the corresponding itineraries offer this route. Road transport, guide language and the border are covered by the full tour terms and must be checked separately.

## Moon Valley excursions near La Paz: a short tour or a journey with Tiwanaku

[Moon Valley near La Paz](/bolivia/place/moon-valley-la-paz/), known as Valle de la Luna, lies in the Mallasa area. Erosion has created sharp clay ridges, pillars and winding passages. In a compact area, visitors can explore a dry landscape strikingly different from the streets and slopes of [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/).

Its main advantage is **the opportunity to combine a nature walk with sightseeing in the city**. You do not need a multi-day Bolivian expedition to visit. However, different excursions may include additional neighborhoods or historic sites, so compare the entire itinerary before choosing.

## Which Ada Tours programs visit Moon Valley?

We offer two options.

- [La Paz and Moon Valley in 4 Hours](/bolivia/la-paz/la-paz-city-moon-valley-four-hours/). This sightseeing route includes views of the city and Illimani mountain, the historic center, the [Witches' Market](/bolivia/place/la-paz-witches-market/) and a walk among the eroded formations of Valle de la Luna. Choose it to see the city and its unusual landscape in one morning or part of a day.
- [La Paz, Moon Valley and Tiwanaku](/bolivia/la-paz/la-paz-moon-valley-tiwanaku/). This itinerary connects city stops and Moon Valley with the [Tiwanaku archaeological site](/bolivia/place/tiwanaku/). It suits travelers whose interest in Bolivia's pre-Columbian culture is as important as its scenery and city neighborhoods.

**The difference is more than duration.** The first option focuses on La Paz and a natural stop. The second adds a separate excursion to archaeological monuments outside the urban area. If you have a flight or transfer afterward, allow sufficient time for the longer route.

## What to see among the clay pinnacles

La Paz's municipal tourism portal describes Valle de la Luna as a landscape of clay formations whose shades vary with the light. Narrow passages, ledges and serrated slopes appear between pale and reddish ridges. Rather than immense mountains, the appeal lies in small features of the terrain: slender peaks, soil layers and shadows inside gullies.

A walk through Moon Valley differs from a normal city viewpoint. In the city you look out across buildings and mountains; in the valley you can approach the eroded formations themselves. For photographs, alternate broad panoramas with close views of individual clay pillars. Staying on marked paths protects visitors and the fragile terrain.

The municipal tourism authority generally recommends April through October for walking because of the drier weather. Check exact opening hours, admission charges and any temporary restrictions for your dates.

## Moon Valley or Tiwanaku: which should you choose?

[Tiwanaku](/bolivia/place/tiwanaku/) offers a different kind of experience: monumental architecture and the heritage of a pre-Columbian civilization. Moon Valley is a geological nature stop near La Paz. The two can be combined in one excursion day, but require more time for travel and sightseeing.

| Format | Main interest |
|---|---|
| La Paz + Moon Valley | City and natural formations |
| La Paz + Tiwanaku | City, nature and archaeology |

If you only have a few hours, the shorter tour leaves time to explore La Paz independently. If you also want to understand Andean history alongside the modern metropolitan area, the longer itinerary offers more.

## Don't confuse the two Moon Valleys

The name Valle de la Luna is used in more than one country. [Moon Valley near La Paz](/bolivia/place/moon-valley-la-paz/) is in Bolivia's suburban Mallasa district. [Moon Valley in the Atacama](/chile/place/moon-valley-atacama/) is a different destination in Chile near San Pedro de Atacama, with different landforms and travel logistics. An excursion to one does not include the other.

For Bolivia itineraries, use the [La Paz excursions catalog](/bolivia/la-paz/) and exact product titles. This is especially helpful when planning a multi-country journey involving both countries.

## What to check before visiting

La Paz is at high altitude, and walks among the clay formations are outdoors. Comfortable shoes, drinking water, sun protection and a layer for the wind are helpful even on a short visit. Travelers with significant mobility restrictions should ask about the paths and number of steps.

When selecting an excursion, check whether admission tickets, transport between stops and your preferred guide language are included. None of these can be inferred simply because a product is called a sightseeing tour.

## Frequently asked questions about Moon Valley excursions

### Can you visit Moon Valley in one day from La Paz?

Yes. It features on the [four-hour La Paz sightseeing excursion](/bolivia/la-paz/la-paz-city-moon-valley-four-hours/). This is a city route with an additional nature stop.

### Is Tiwanaku included in the four-hour tour?

No. The [Tiwanaku itinerary](/bolivia/la-paz/la-paz-moon-valley-tiwanaku/) is a different product with an archaeological section and additional timing requirements.

### What scenery awaits in the valley?

Narrow clay ridges, pillars, gullies and soil whose shades change with the light. It is a dry eroded landscape, unlike the high-altitude lakes of the Altiplano.

### When is the best time for walking?

Municipal tourism information recommends the relatively dry months of April through October. Actual weather, trail conditions and access rules matter for a specific day.

### Is this the same Moon Valley as in Chile?

No. [Bolivia's Moon Valley](/bolivia/place/moon-valley-la-paz/) is near La Paz, while [Chile's](/chile/place/moon-valley-atacama/) is in the Atacama Desert. They are covered by separate excursions.

## Eduardo Avaroa: from the red lagoon to the green

The [Eduardo Avaroa National Reserve](/bolivia/place/eduardo-avaroa-national-reserve/) is in southwestern Bolivia, in the high Andes. Dry desert plains, unusual rock formations, mineral lakes and geothermal areas lie close together. The Ada Tours excursion visits the region's most distinctive natural attractions in **one full day**, beginning near [Ojo de Perdiz](/bolivia/place/ojo-de-perdiz/).

Our route includes **the Stone Tree, Siloli Desert, Laguna Colorada, Sol de Mañana, Polques Hot Springs and Laguna Verde**. After the sightseeing stops, there is a transfer toward Uyuni. Despite the proximity of the Chilean border, crossing it is not part of this itinerary.

## The Stone Tree and the Siloli Desert

An early departure takes travelers to the [Stone Tree](/bolivia/place/arbol-de-piedra/), one of the best-known rock formations in the Siloli Desert. Its narrow base and broader upper section were shaped by prolonged wind erosion. The distinctive form stands out against the vast desert plateau.

**Siloli** is worth seeing in its own right, with broad views across rocky expanses and mountain ranges. It is a high-altitude desert, so even short walks on dry ground involve wind, intense sunshine and potentially cold temperatures.

Unlike a city or developed park, individual stops here have little infrastructure for an extended stay. Prioritize safe movement along the route and adequate time for photographs.

## Why Laguna Colorada is red

[Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/) is famous for the unusual reddish, terracotta tones of its water, associated with microorganisms and natural deposits. The visible intensity depends on weather, light and lake conditions, so do not expect an identical view in every season.

The lagoon and surrounding areas are also a habitat for high-altitude birds, including flamingos. But nobody can predict exactly where or when wildlife will appear. Watch from a distance and follow conservation rules. A dedicated ornithological excursion, optical equipment and a guaranteed number of sightings are not promised.

There is relatively little cultural sightseeing on this day: the main attractions are geology, natural colors and Andean ecosystems. For more nature-focused travel, browse [wildlife and nature journeys](/interests/wildlife/).

## Sol de Mañana: the geothermal field

After the red lagoon, the itinerary heads to **Sol de Mañana**. Columns of steam rise from the ground; high temperatures and geothermal activity make the landscape particularly unusual. It is a natural area with potentially dangerous hot ground and water.

Visitors must keep to permitted areas, follow their guides and avoid approaching steam vents or mud formations for photographs. Although it may resemble hot springs, the boiling geothermal ground is not suitable for bathing.

The next stop is **Polques**, known for its hot springs. They are included in the route, but bathing, admission tickets, towels and separate spa services require confirmation. If you would like to bathe, check whether it is possible and under what terms beforehand.

## Laguna Verde and Licancabur volcano

[Laguna Verde](/bolivia/place/laguna-verde/) lies at the foot of Licancabur volcano near the Chilean border. Its mineral-rich water takes on greenish tones that change with the wind and light. Against the volcano's near-perfect cone, the scene differs greatly from terracotta-colored Laguna Colorada.

Seeing the volcano on the horizon does not mean climbing it. Nor does proximity to the border mean entry into Chile is included: after the lagoon, the itinerary returns toward **Uyuni** and continues through Bolivia.

For any broader multi-country itinerary, check travel documents and border rules separately for each traveler's nationality and the actual route. This excursion day itself does not cross the border.

## Preparing for a day at high altitude

Altitude, dry air, wind and long distances between stops are the main considerations. Bring warm outerwear, sunglasses, a hat, water and shoes with non-slip soles. A warm jacket is important even when the sunshine feels comfortable.

Our program includes **lunch on the road** and a private transfer to Uyuni Airport. On the linked 15-day tour, the flight to La Paz is planned for the following day; this does not guarantee a flight immediately after visiting Laguna Verde. Confirm transfer times, the overnight stay and any restrictions in the current itinerary.

If you are starting from the [Uyuni area](/bolivia/place/uyuni/), the first stage can be the [route through the Valley of Rocks to Ojo de Perdiz](/bolivia/uyuni/uyuni-south-lipez-ojo-de-perdiz/). Then continue to the red and green lagoons. This division helps you select a [Bolivia tour](/bolivia/tour/) by the actual number of days spent at altitude rather than simply by photographs of the salt flats.

## Frequently asked questions about the Eduardo Avaroa reserve

### Can you see both colorful lagoons in one day?

On this excursion, Laguna Colorada and Laguna Verde are included in the same full-day itinerary. Stop durations depend on travel logistics and road conditions.

### Can you bathe at Sol de Mañana?

No. The geothermal field, with hot steam and ground, is not a bathing site. Polques Hot Springs are a separate stop, and bathing arrangements there must be confirmed.

### Does the excursion cross the Chilean border?

No. Laguna Verde is near the border, but the itinerary continues within Bolivia toward Uyuni.

### Are flamingo sightings guaranteed?

No. Wildlife populations and viewing conditions change; no guaranteed birdwatching encounters are offered as part of the service.
